title: Low engine oil pressure
fullDescription:
New Holland tractors with FPT/CNH engines monitor oil pressure via SPN 100. FMI 1 indicates pressure below allowable minimum and the ECU will derate the engine to protect bearings.

Check oil level and grade first; failed sensor or pump are next.

fixSteps.title: Check oil level
fixSteps.instruction: Verify with dipstick on level ground, top up to spec.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Read live data — sensor should show ~50 PSI hot at idle.

whenToCallPro: If oil pump replacement is required.
videoSearchQuery: New Holland SPN 100 oil pressure fix

faq.a: Stop immediately — running with low oil pressure damages bearings.

title: Engine coolant temperature high
fullDescription:
FMI 0 means coolant is above the upper threshold. ECU will derate and eventually shut down to prevent damage.

Check coolant level, radiator screen for chaff, and operation of fan and thermostat.

fixSteps.title: Clean radiator screen
fixSteps.instruction: Open hood, blow out chaff with compressed air.

title: DPF regeneration required
fullDescription:
Tier 4 New Holland tractors use a DPF that must periodically burn off soot. Frequent low-load operation prevents passive regen, and a manual or service regen is required.

SPN 3216 with high FMI indicates regen has been deferred too long.

fixSteps.title: Initiate manual regen
fixSteps.instruction: Use dash menu to start a parked regen — typically 30-45 min.

fixSteps.title: Increase load operation
fixSteps.instruction: Run tractor under load to keep DPF hot.

whenToCallPro: If DPF needs cleaning at dealer.
videoSearchQuery: New Holland T6 DPF regen procedure

faq.a: Don't — eventually DPF clogs and requires expensive service cleaning.

title: DEF dosing system fault
shortDescription: Diesel Exhaust Fluid injector or pump fault.
fullDescription:
SCR-equipped tractors meter DEF into exhaust to convert NOx. SPN 3361 indicates the dosing valve is not operating correctly — clogged, electrical fault, or pump failure.

DEF crystallization is the most common cause, especially after extended idle.

fixSteps.title: Replace DEF
fixSteps.instruction: Drain old DEF and refill with fresh ISO 22241 fluid.

fixSteps.title: Service injector
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and inspect dosing injector for crystals.

videoSearchQuery: New Holland DEF dosing fault SPN 3361

faq.a: 12 months sealed; 6 months open in cool storage.

title: PTO will not engage
shortDescription: Rear PTO fails to engage when switch pressed.
fullDescription:
Modern NH tractors use electro-hydraulic PTO clutches with a solenoid valve and pressure switches. Fault can be electrical, hydraulic, or operator-related.

Check operator presence on seat, range lever in proper position, and that PTO speed switch is set.

fixSteps.title: Verify operator on seat
fixSteps.instruction: Sit firmly, ensure seat switch is engaged.

fixSteps.title: Test solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Use diagnostic to actuate PTO solenoid manually.

whenToCallPro: If hydraulic pressure low or clutch pack worn.
videoSearchQuery: New Holland PTO won't engage fix

faq.a: No — engine must be running with hydraulic pressure.

title: Three-point hitch will not raise
shortDescription: Rear hitch does not respond to control.
fullDescription:
NH 3-point uses an electro-hydraulic Lift-O-Matic system. Failure to raise can be control input, position sensor, valve, or low hydraulic flow.

Check position knob, transport lock, and load setting.
videoSearchQuery: New Holland 3 point hitch wont raise

faq.a: Varies by model — typically 3000-6000 lb at lift points.

title: Transmission shift fault
shortDescription: Power Shuttle or Power Shift will not change ranges.
fullDescription:
Electro-hydraulic shifting transmissions can throw faults from solenoid failures, low hydraulic pressure, or speed sensor issues.

Most faults log SPN 191 or SPN 524. Read codes with NH ESM tool.

fixSteps.title: Check fluid level
fixSteps.instruction: Verify transmission oil at correct level.

fixSteps.title: Read codes
fixSteps.instruction: Pull DTCs and address specific solenoid.

title: Hydraulic pressure below threshold
shortDescription: Loader and remotes weak or non-functional.
fullDescription:
Hydraulic pump on NH tractors maintains 2500-3000 PSI. Worn pump, low fluid, or clogged filter can drop pressure.

Check filter first — most common cause.

faq.a: NH 134D or NH Ambra Multi-G — do not mix.

title: Engine will not start
fullDescription:
Common-rail diesel engines need fuel pressure, glow plugs (if cold), and proper start enable signals. Air in fuel system after running out of fuel is a top issue.

Bleed fuel system, check fuel filter, verify glow plug operation in cold weather.

fixSteps.title: Replace fuel filter
fixSteps.instruction: Change main fuel filter and water separator.

fixSteps.title: Bleed fuel system
fixSteps.instruction: Use hand primer until air is gone.

videoSearchQuery: New Holland diesel wont start bleed fuel

faq.a: Always bleed system after running out of fuel.

title: Glow plug system fault
fullDescription:
ECU monitors current draw of glow plug relay. Open or shorted glow plug logs SPN 676. Cold-weather starting will be poor or impossible.

Test each glow plug for resistance (typically 0.5-1.5 ohm).
whenToCallPro: If plug is seized in head.
videoSearchQuery: New Holland glow plug replace SPN 676

faq.a: Wait full pre-heat cycle before cranking, especially below 32 deg F.
